correctness.rationale: Every equal-degree pair contributes zero and every other pair at most one. Among the larger guild of \(b=qa+r\) vertices, degrees lie in \(1,\ldots,a\); discrete convexity forces at least \((a-r) inom q2+r inom{q+1}2\) ties. Constructing the nested Ferrers incidence matrix with exactly balanced multiplicities makes every other pair contribute one, reaching the bound. At equality row neighborhoods must be a strict nested chain and the longer-guild degree histogram balanced, proving the complete classification. The packaged verifier checks 176554 matrices exhaustively and all maximizers for ten finite shapes, plus numerous larger constructed cases using exact integer arithmetic.

evidence: Britton et al., Biomath 4 (2015), Section II.A (printed pages 3–6), formalizes NODF and proves that index one is possible only for a square full-triangular matrix and that index zero has a componentwise degree characterization.
Song et al. (2017) use a greedy algorithm to approximate maximum NODF subject to observed link count and both guild sizes.
Hoeppke and Simmons (2021), Introduction and Description, explicitly pose maxima with the number of rows, columns, AND links fixed and propose numerical heuristics, not a shape-only all-edge optimum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier square-case maximum is a special case recovered by the new formula, not a new discovery. The fixed-link optimizations yield values no larger than the dimension-only maximum but do not state or imply its exact closed form or its global maximizing family.

originality.rationale: The NODF definition and the square maximum-one characterization are explicitly prior results. No inspected primary source or targeted search located an exact dimension-only NODF maximum for all rectangular shapes, its balanced-degree Ferrers classification, or the isomorphism type count. Published fixed-edge-count maximization concerns a strictly more constrained optimization for each link count and reports heuristics rather than a closed universal rectangular formula; it does not itself imply the new equality classification.
residual_risks: A differently phrased combinatorial or software result might state the same dimension-only NODF maximum without being indexed by NODF-specific searches.
Real ecological networks have a fixed link count; the shape-only optimum is an upper bound and may be unattainable at empirical connectance.
Tied-degree pair conventions, isolated species, weighted entries, and alternative pair denominators change the claimed optimization problem.

value.rationale: NODF is used to quantify nestedness of empirical ecological bipartite networks and is known to have misleading comparisons without structural normalization. The derived sharp dimension-only ceiling isolates a constraint caused solely by rectangular guild imbalance; the balanced Ferrers family exhibits all attainable sharp architectures. Its exact formula and nonvanishing asymptotic penalty yield scientifically motivated baselines and upper-bound sanity checks without pretending to solve the distinct fixed-link optimization problem.
